entries.title: No accountable risk owner

problem.statement: No named person is responsible for accepting residual risk, funding remediation or stopping deployment.
problem.customer_symptom: Operators cannot identify who is accountable for accepting residual risk, authorising remediation or stopping deployment, so material security decisions may remain unresolved, be made informally, or be attributed to someone without the required authority.
problem.credible_failure_or_attack: governance failure can leave a material risk, unresolved finding or deployment decision without a named accountable human who has documented authority to accept residual risk, authorise remediation or stop or withhold deployment.
problem.severity_rationale: Default high rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: missing ownership, ambiguous responsibility, expired appointment, incomplete delegation or unsupported decision authority
problem.trust_boundary: The control governs the boundary between technical assessment evidence and the human governance authority responsible for accepting risk, authorising remediation and stopping or withholding deployment.
problem.operational_impact: Without an accountable risk owner, critical findings, remediation funding, residual-risk acceptance and deployment holds may have no authorised decision-maker, causing unresolved risk, delayed response or unsupported deployment decisions.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Appoint a named accountable risk owner for the exact assessed system and scope. Document the owner's role, contact, effective date, expiry where applicable, and explicit authority for residual-risk acceptance, remediation funding or authorisation, and deployment stop or withholding. Define deputies or delegation only where their authority and scope are explicitly recorded.

problem.statement: The organisation has not stated which users, decisions, sectors or actions the agent must never support.
problem.customer_symptom: Operators cannot determine which users, decisions, sectors, actions or outcomes the agent must never support, so prohibited or harmful behaviour may be treated as ordinary in-scope use.

affected_assets: people, rights and safety affected by agent actions
problem.severity_rationale: Default critical rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
applicability: agents affecting people, rights, safety or regulated activity
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: missing or ambiguous prohibited-use rules, incomplete harm analysis, unsafe requests, model behaviour, tool execution or operator error

entries.title: Risk classification does not match real impact

problem.statement: The agent is treated as low risk even though it can move money, alter records, affect rights, disclose sensitive data or control infrastructure.
problem.customer_symptom: The system is governed as lower risk than its actual reachable capabilities justify, so controls, review depth, evidence requirements or deployment gates may be weaker than the maximum credible impact requires.
problem.credible_failure_or_attack: an incomplete or outdated risk classification can omit impact-relevant capabilities such as authority, sensitive-data access, irreversible actions, financial effects, effects on people or rights, infrastructure control, scale or downstream dependency chains, causing the declared risk tier to understate the system's real maximum credible impact.
affected_assets: people, rights and safety affected by agent actions
problem.severity_rationale: Default critical rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
applicability: agents with tools or consequential outputs
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: incomplete capability inventory, outdated classification evidence, underestimated impact, configuration drift or human classification error
problem.trust_boundary: The control governs the boundary between the agent's actual reachable authority and impact and the governance classification used to determine required controls, testing, evidence and deployment decisions.
problem.operational_impact: If the declared risk tier understates real impact, the system may receive weaker controls, testing or review than its capabilities require. The affected classification and deployment decision must remain on hold until impact is reassessed and an accountable human records the resulting tier.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Reclassify the system using evidence of actual reachable authority, assets, data exposure, maximum action values, reversibility, scale, affected people and downstream dependency chains. Bind the resulting tier and rationale to the exact assessed version and require accountable human approval of any classification decision.

entries.title: Trust boundaries and data flows are undocumented

problem.statement: Reviewers cannot see where untrusted input becomes model context, where identities change, or where outputs reach tools and external systems.
problem.customer_symptom: Reviewers cannot reliably determine how inputs, model context, memory, tools, data stores, identities, network destinations, human approvals and evidence stores connect, so important trust-boundary crossings or data flows may be missed during assessment.
problem.credible_failure_or_attack: an undocumented or stale architecture path can allow untrusted input, model output, sensitive data, authority or tool execution to cross a trust boundary without being visible to reviewers, causing controls to be applied to the wrong component or leaving a material path outside the assessment.
affected_assets: human approval points and authority boundaries
problem.severity_rationale: Default high rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: incomplete architecture documentation, stale data-flow mapping, undocumented integration, hidden execution path, configuration drift or review error
problem.trust_boundary: The control governs whether all material crossings between users, agents, models, tools, stores, networks, approval authorities and evidence stores are explicitly identified and traceable for the exact assessed version.
problem.operational_impact: If trust boundaries and data flows are incomplete or stale, reviewers may miss where untrusted input enters, where authority changes, where sensitive data moves, or where model output reaches consequential systems, making downstream security conclusions incomplete or unreliable.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Create and maintain a versioned architecture model for the exact assessed system. Document material actors, trust zones, data flows, models, memory, tools, stores, network destinations, authority boundaries, approval points and evidence paths. Bind the model to implementation evidence and update it whenever material architecture or scope changes.

entries.title: Data classification is absent or inconsistent

problem.statement: Prompts, memories, logs and tool arguments may contain personal, confidential, regulated or secret data without suitable handling rules.
problem.customer_symptom: The system handles personal, confidential, regulated or secret data without a consistent classification and handling model, so restricted data may enter model context, logs, tools, storage or exports under rules intended for less sensitive data.
problem.credible_failure_or_attack: unclassified or misclassified data can be routed to an incompatible destination, retained too long, exposed in logs or model context, written to an unsafe location, or exported when its handling policy should have required redaction, denial or restriction.
affected_assets: personal, confidential, regulated and secret data
problem.severity_rationale: Default high rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: missing classification, inconsistent labels, incomplete propagation, misclassification, policy drift or handling rules that do not match the data class
problem.trust_boundary: The control governs the boundary between data classification and every destination where that data may be processed, persisted, transmitted, displayed or exported.
problem.operational_impact: If data classification is absent or inconsistent, restricted information may be processed under weaker rules than intended, requiring containment, evidence review, correction of handling rules and retest before the affected path can be trusted.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Define and maintain a versioned data-classification and handling policy. Classify data before or at entry to material processing paths, propagate or recompute classification where needed, and enforce class-appropriate redaction, denial, retention and export rules at each relevant destination.

entries.title: Security-relevant changes bypass review

problem.statement: Prompt, model, tool, policy or data-source changes can reach production without threat modelling, tests or approval.
problem.customer_symptom: A security-relevant production change can become authoritative without the required classification, review, testing, accountable approval or exact-version deployment evidence.

problem.severity_rationale: Default high rating reflects the potential impact before customer-specific exposure, likelihood, reversibility and compensating controls are verified.
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: unreviewed production change, stale approval reuse, version substitution, deployment drift, incomplete change classification or release-process failure
problem.trust_boundary: The control governs the transition from a proposed security-relevant change to the authoritative production artefact, including review, testing, approval, version binding, deployment provenance and reassessment.
problem.operational_impact: If a security-relevant change bypasses review or inherits stale approval, an unassessed artefact may become authoritative in production. The affected release or deployment decision must remain on hold until the exact version is reviewed, tested and approved.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Classify security-relevant changes; require appropriate review and negative tests; bind approvals and evidence to immutable versions or artefact digests; enforce reviewed deployment provenance; trigger reassessment after material scope or architecture changes; and maintain a known-good rollback version.

entries.title: Shadow or experimental agents reach real data

problem.statement: A prototype, notebook, personal API key or unofficial agent can reach production data, tools or services outside approved controls.
problem.customer_symptom: Operators discover experimental or unofficial AI components using real production endpoints, customer data, provider accounts or service credentials without the approved inventory, identity, network, logging or change-control path.

problem.trust_boundary: The relevant trust boundary separates approved experimentation and sandbox environments from production identities, data stores, tools, networks and provider accounts; experimental components must not cross it except through an explicitly governed production path.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Separate experimentation from production with distinct accounts, projects, networks and credentials; provide governed sandboxes with synthetic data; block unapproved providers and routes; prohibit personal credentials for production access; and rotate exposed shadow credentials after containment.

entries.title: External destinations and egress paths are unknown

problem.statement: The agent can send data to domains, webhooks or tools that are absent from the threat model.
problem.customer_symptom: An operator cannot account for every external domain, IP, webhook, tool endpoint, callback or proxy route the assessed agent can reach, creating an unreviewed path for data disclosure, unintended external interaction or policy bypass.

external domains, IP addresses, webhooks and callbacks

problem.severity_rationale: Unknown or uncontrolled egress can enable data disclosure or unintended interaction with external systems. Final severity depends on reachable destinations, transmitted data, available actions, exposure, reversibility and compensating controls.
problem.threat_actor_or_failure_source: untrusted input, unsafe agent behaviour, compromised tool or dependency, configuration drift, or operator error
problem.trust_boundary: The boundary between the assessed agent or tool runtime and external network destinations, downstream services, webhooks, callbacks and other outbound routes.
problem.operational_impact: An undocumented or uncontrolled outbound path can expose scoped data, reach an unapproved service or bypass expected network controls. Operators may need to disable the route, investigate transmitted data and destinations, update the architecture inventory and repeat testing against the corrected version.

solution_summary.recommended_remediation: Maintain an explicit destination and egress inventory; enforce deny-by-default outbound policy using controlled proxy, firewall or equivalent enforcement; apply destination allowlists and DNS/IP validation; constrain dynamic destinations; and record privacy-aware runtime egress evidence.
